status.en: 25 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 56% more than the week before, most of them in Tigray, Amhara and Addis Ababa.
status.nb: 25 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 56 prosent flere enn uken før, flest i Tigray, Amhara og Addis Ababa.

summary.en: Armed attackers killed at least 60 Orthodox Christians in two separate incidents in Oromia and a drone strike killed two government civil servants in western Oromia. Senior Tigray Military Commander Major General Yohannes was captured near the Eritrean border. Ethiopia received delivery of 12 Russian Su-35 fighter jets and plans for S-400 air defenses amid rising tensions with Eritrea. Up to 50,000 Ethiopians have fled across the Kenya border into Moyale County. 2,824 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Væpnede angripere drepte minst 60 ortodokse kristne i to separate hendelser i Oromia, og et droneangrep drepte to sivile tjenestemenn i vestlige Oromia. Den senior tigrayiske militærkommandanten major general Yohannes ble tatt til fange nær grensen mot Eritrea. Etiopia mottok levering av 12 russiske Su‑35 jagerfly og planlegger S‑400 luftforsvar midt i økende spenninger med Eritrea. Opptil 50 000 etiopiere har flyktet over Kenyas grense til Moyale fylke. 2 824 dødsfall i kamper i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Fano insurgency
background.extract: The Fano insurgency is an armed conflict and insurgency in the Amhara Region of Ethiopia that began in April 2023 between the Fano militia and the Ethiopian government. The conflict started after the government attempted to dissolve the Amhara Special Forces and other regional forces as part of a plan to reform and centralize the country's security apparatus, and integrate them into the federal armed forces. This move led to protests and armed resistance by local forces under Fano.
